Wind turbines provided almost 8.4% of the total generated electricity in the United States in 2020.
More than 700,800 wind turbines are running across 44 states in the United States.
The authors used SolidWorks 2021 to design 3D models of the wind turbine blades with 40 different defect variations.
The authors used the Unity Perception Package to capture synthetic images with variations in background, camera angle, and lighting effects.
The authors trained a U-Net model, a popular convolutional neural network for image segmentation, using the synthetic images and their corresponding semantic segmentation ground truth labels.
The authors obtained a Dice Coefficient of 0.658 for the U-Net model, indicating moderate segmentation accuracy.
The Dice Loss function is calculated as 1 - Dice Coefficient, where the Dice Coefficient measures the overlap between the predicted segmentation mask and the ground truth mask.
The authors plan to work on improving the U-Net model for better segmentation accuracy and adding a classification module.
The authors also plan to investigate the approach using a wider range of defects and real wind turbine images.
The proposed approach can generate a large volume of synthetic training data, which is useful when real-world data is limited or expensive to obtain.
The proposed approach allows for automated and efficient defect detection, reducing the time and cost of manual inspections.
The authors used Google Colab for model training and testing.
The authors used the Adam optimizer, a well-known optimization algorithm for deep neural network training.
The authors divided the dataset into 75% for training and 25% for testing.
The authors trained the U-Net model for 100 epochs.
